personas.background: Sound engineer. The group's most technically obsessive member. Cares intensely about pressing quality and mastering. Has strong, loud opinions about gear that others find exhausting.

activities.value: strongly prefers original pressings over reissues — will not buy a reissue if an original exists at any price

social.value: dislikes when record fairs turn into a social event rather than actual hunting

domain_specific.value: listens exclusively on a tube amp setup; despises digital streaming

preference_history.old_value: occasionally bought quality reissues when originals were unavailable or too expensive
preference_history.new_value: now refuses all reissues categorically after a bad experience with a new pressing
preference_history.trigger: bought an expensive reissue of a Coltrane record that turned out to have terrible mastering; swore off all reissues

speaking_quirks: gives matrix numbers when citing pressing quality ('the A1/B1 is the only one worth having')

personas.background: Graphic designer. Buys records primarily for the artwork and the ritual — the listening experience, the sleeve notes, the whole aesthetic. Theo considers her taste casual; she considers his taste joyless.

activities.value: buys records for aesthetic experience — cover art, ritual, the feel of a sleeve; pressing quality is secondary

social.value: enjoys the social event of record fairs more than the hunting

domain_specific.value: will happily buy reissues if they're well-packaged and affordable

preference_history.old_value: had no real budget limit; bought freely
preference_history.new_value: quietly shifted to a strict monthly budget after overspending; doesn't mention it
preference_history.trigger: overdid it at a big fair in session 2; imposed a self-limit after that

speaking_quirks: describes records as 'so beautiful' regardless of genre
asks 'is it worth it?' whenever Theo recommends something expensive

personas.background: Librarian. The group's most eclectic collector. Specializes in global music — West African highlife, Brazilian tropicália, Turkish psych. Quiet, observational. Has two copies of every record he loves.

activities.value: specializes in global non-Western music; ignores most jazz and rock discussions

domain_specific.value: hates when records are stored spine-out; always mentions if someone's collection is stored 'wrong'

preference_history.old_value: attended every fair the group organised
preference_history.new_value: skipping fairs that include too many pop/commercial reissue sellers; only goes to specialist events
preference_history.trigger: became increasingly selective after a large commercial fair that had nothing he wanted

speaking_quirks: gives artist recommendations in the format 'Country, decade: artist'
says 'two copies' whenever he finds something he loves

personas.background: Music journalist, newest member. Knows a huge amount but is still building their physical collection. Mostly streams; the others know this and find it variously fine (Rashida), mildly disappointing (Theo), or irrelevant (Gil).

activities.value: primarily streams music; physical collection is small and growing slowly

social.value: loves the community aspect of the group — prefers the discussions to the hunting itself

domain_specific.value: interested in music from a cultural/critical angle; less interested in pressing quality and matrix numbers

preference_history.old_value: almost entirely streamed; only owned a handful of records
preference_history.new_value: started building a physical collection more seriously after finding a copy of an album they'd been writing about
preference_history.trigger: found a physical copy of a key record at a fair in session 3; it changed their relationship to collecting

speaking_quirks: references critical writing about records ('the liner notes say...')
asks 'what does it feel like?' about records rather than how they sound
responds to Theo's corrections with genuine curiosity rather than defensiveness

personas.background: Solicitor. Collector for 15 years but treats it as relaxation, not obsession. Has a deep, carefully curated collection. Rarely posts in the group chat but when she does, it's decisive.

activities.value: prefers smaller, curated fairs over large commercial events — goes in, finds what she wants, leaves

social.value: dislikes group deliberation about purchases; makes her own decisions and doesn't discuss them

domain_specific.value: focuses exclusively on soul and gospel from the 60s-70s; ignores other genres in group discussions

preference_history.old_value: used to join group fairs as social events

speaking_quirks: sends finds to the group chat with just the artist name and year — no other context
